entries.title: Espionage, AI, and the Risks of Strategic Overreaction
entries.summary: Recent allegations that Nvidia's CEO was targeted by Chinese intelligence raised concerns about US-China technology competition. However, the public record remains incomplete and doesn't prove technology transfer or warrant specific policy changes. The piece warns against strategic overreaction that could weaken the AI ecosystem whilst failing to protect sensitive capabilities.

entries.title: The Rebirth of Neo-Nazi Ideology in Russia and Its Appeal to Young People
entries.summary: Russia's neo-Nazi violence, previously suppressed through enforcement, has resurged since 2022's Ukraine invasion. Hate-motivated crimes spiked from under 100 victims in 2015 to over 250 in 2024, with perpetrators often aged 13-14. The NS/WP Crew online group actively recruits young people to neo-Nazi ideology through Russian-language social media.

entries.title: NCSC scheme will help critical organisations test their cyber defences
entries.summary: NCSC launches a new Cyber Adversary Simulation scheme enabling critical organisations to test their cybersecurity resilience through rigorous, real-world exercises conducted by trusted external providers.

entries.title: Cogent and OpenAI build cyber defense factories for enterprises
entries.summary: Cogent integrates OpenAI models with enterprise data to enable automated vulnerability remediation using AI agents, creating cyber defence capabilities for businesses.

entries.title: The supermarket fridge hack exposes the cracks in tech vision of an ‘internet of things’
entries.summary: Hackers remotely compromised refrigeration systems at hundreds of European supermarkets in October-November 2026, spoiling food worth millions of euros. France accused Iran; others suspect Russia. The incident reveals internet-connected devices' vulnerability and raises questions about responsibility for securing interconnected physical systems.

entries.title: Poland shuts down government services platform ePUAP following cyberattack
entries.summary: Poland shut down its ePUAP government services platform following a cyberattack. The system allows citizens to submit documents, communicate with agencies and complete administrative procedures online.

entries.title: Britain, France set out first guidelines for commercial hacking firms
entries.summary: Britain and France released initial guidelines for commercial hacking firms, requiring customer vetting, technical safeguards against misuse and systems for monitoring and reporting abuse.

entries.title: A 13-Year-Old Asked AI About Suicide on Her School Laptop. It Didn’t Get Flagged for Weeks
entries.summary: A 13-year-old used Google's Gemini AI via her school Chromebook to plan suicide, but the school's monitoring systems failed to flag the activity for weeks, according to her parents' allegations.

entries.title: Google Cloud pins London outage on PLC misconfiguration
entries.summary: Google has traced the 20 October power failure that knocked out UK banks, courts and couriers to a programmable logic controller (PLC) that measured mains voltage on the wrong side of a circuit breaker – a single sensing error that stopped the site’s emergency generators from starting and let…

entries.title: Closing the AI guidance gap in education
entries.summary: New ThinkYoung research and lessons from OpenAI’s EMEA education partnerships on supporting teachers, AI literacy, and independent learning.

entries.title: Work at the Frontier: AI’s effect on freelance work
entries.summary: New research from OpenAI and Upwork finds shifting demand for freelance work, new skill combinations, and larger budgets and more hours for AI-related projects.

entries.title: Jensen Huang: The Spy Who Shagged Me (allegedly)
entries.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been getting around a bit. He had a girlfriend on the side and it’s hit the papers. This is not anyone’s business — except that the alleged girlfriend is allegedly a spy for China. And the US alleges she got Jensen to sell Nvidia chips…

entries.title: I asked every TV manufacturer 17 questions about how they spy on you
entries.summary: Every TV company is spying on you , not just LG. Like other tech companies, they collect lots of information, and while some is necessary for products to work, not all of it is - and could include details you'd prefer to keep private. Many customers are concerned about how…

entries.title: Duolingo, Strava, and Ticketmaster Are All Caught Up in EU’s New Digital Fairness Rules
entries.summary: Winning streaks can be turned off and influencers will be forced to reveal when they’re being paid under the new Digital Fairness Act aimed at tackling “dark patterns” on platforms and services.

entries.title: Diluting Poisoned Fine-Tuning Data Can Strengthen Its Effect
entries.summary: Title covers diluting poisoned fine-tuning data and its effects on AI models. No text supplied; unable to provide specific findings or claims.

entries.title: The U.S.–China AI Competition: Two Paths to Artificial General Intelligence
entries.summary: Report comparing US and Chinese approaches to artificial general intelligence. US focuses on human-level reasoning across tasks; China emphasises embodied AI grounded in physical and social systems. US leads in semiconductors and frontier models; China has engineering capacity and deployment scale.

entries.title: Europe faces faster cyberattacks than ever. But many of the solutions are long known
entries.summary: Title indicates Europe faces accelerating cyberattacks but established solutions exist. No text supplied; unable to provide specific findings or claims.

entries.title: Data dive: Mapping UK councils’ hyperscale dependence
entries.summary: DNS scan of 382 UK councils' infrastructure finds near-universal dependence on US hyperscalers. 99% of council domains route to Microsoft, AWS or Google; 51% of routable records sit on these providers, with Microsoft accounting for roughly 70%.

entries.title: A chilling warning of AI-powered cyber attacks
entries.summary: Issue covers National Cyber Security Centre warning on AI-powered cyber attacks, public cloud carbon footprint and costs, and lessons from Ukraine's tech sector during wartime.

entries.title: Anti-Technology Narratives That May Lead to Violence Spread Online
entries.summary: Anti-technology and anti-AI sentiments online can radicalise toward violence, with AI becoming a focal point for extremist ideologies. Content spreads via social media as radicalisation pathway, ranging from anarcho-primitivism to targeted violence against AI technology.

entries.title: Anthropic’s Safety Mission vs. Public-Company Pressure, November 10
entries.summary: Title addresses tension between Anthropic's safety mission and public-company pressures. No text supplied; unable to provide specific findings or claims.

entries.title: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI
entries.summary: Scott Wiener, newly elected California congressman, prioritises AI regulation, citing recursive self-improvement concerns. Previously authored California AI bills; received funding from AI regulation nonprofit; advocates slowing AI development through federal legislation.

entries.title: The incidence of con- tent that is harmful to children on regulated services
entries.summary: Ofcom report on the prevalence of content harmful to children on regulated services. No text supplied; unable to summarise findings.

entries.title: Control Room: A central system to track and stop model workloads across our research infrastructure
entries.summary: OpenAI describes Control Room, a system tracking model workloads across its research infrastructure that can rapidly halt them when safety or security concerns emerge.

entries.title: News AFP sounds alarm as youth terror caseload surges despite social media ban ABC News (Australia)
entries.summary: Australian Federal Police report rising youth terrorism caseload despite social media restrictions. No text supplied; unable to provide specific findings.

entries.title: Stephanie Johanssen: Police boards play a vital role in AI oversight – but they don’t need to be tech experts
entries.summary: Stephanie Johanssen argues police boards play an important role in AI oversight but need not comprise technology experts. No text supplied; unable to summarise arguments.

entries.title: UK MPs Push Mandatory Software To Scan Every Phone Image
entries.summary: Cross-party UK MPs and peers propose mandatory software on all phones and tablets to scan images for child sexual abuse material and AI-generated content, including livestreams. Conservative peer John Nash leads the effort; Labour MP Jess Phillips supports it.

entries.title: Sarajevo and Vukovar to Kharkiv and Mariupol: The Evolution of Urbicide in Modern Warfare
entries.summary: Paper examines urbicide—deliberate targeting of cities and urban infrastructure—comparing destruction in Sarajevo and Vukovar during Yugoslav wars with Kharkiv and Mariupol in Ukraine, tracking evolution from artillery-based sieges to rapid bombardment via missiles and drones.

entries.title: Why VPNs Are Worth Defending
entries.summary: VPN developers report Apple App Store removals in Russia as government crackdowns intensify. Russia has blocked FaceTime, added Apple and Microsoft to surveillance registry, and restricted opposition media, leaving citizens with diminishing options for uncensored communication.

entries.title: US Army member arrested in UK over allegations of spying for Russia
entries.summary: Unnamed US Army soldier arrested in UK by British counterterrorism police working with FBI and military on espionage allegations involving Russia.

entries.title: Palantir exec nominated to lead CISA; lame-duck Senate vote is uncertain
entries.summary: Michael LoSapio, Palantir's chief information security officer, has been officially nominated by President Donald Trump to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Senate confirmation vote timing remains uncertain.

entries.title: The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot. We Asked 10 Experts What the Real Nightmares Are
entries.summary: Article discusses genuine AI risks with ten experts, identifying nuclear catastrophe and China–US competition as real concerns. Dismisses apocalyptic scenarios like Skynet as misplaced focus.

entries.title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
entries.summary: DeepMind researchers formally verified that the Signal encryption protocol functions as intended. Their stated goal is to formally verify all software globally.

entries.title: Come and Take It
entries.summary: Covers AI companies restricting reverse-engineering capabilities in their tools.

entries.title: 'Reverse Engineer Anything': AI Companies Crack Down on the Coolest Thing People Were Doing With AI
entries.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI have restricted using Claude and Codex for AI-powered reverse engineering, blocking users attempting to modify owned devices. Users report account limitations and bans. Decomp.wtf project shut down. Users previously used these tools to unbrick devices, modify smart TVs and install alternative software.

entries.title: Bad news for kinky Brits
entries.summary: UK implemented strict new pornography law criminalising certain acts including breath play, choking and strangulation, even privately recorded. Penalties include up to five years prison. Sex workers report mass content removal from platforms with little notice, causing significant economic disruption.

entries.title: Marking a milestone for our non-contact sexual offences training
entries.summary: College of Policing marks milestone achievement in non-contact sexual offences training programme.

entries.title: Gartner Symposium: Who is in control of AI?
entries.summary: Historian Yuval Noah Harari addressed Gartner Symposium, arguing AI differs fundamentally from other inventions as it makes independent decisions and cannot be controlled like tools. Warned AI capability may exceed human comprehension as systems advance.

entries.title: Google Cloud London outage: Continuity lessons for IT leaders
entries.summary: Google Cloud's London datacentre outage on 20 October took one of three availability zones offline, disrupting major organisations and court video systems. Google's preliminary report found secondary failover and queuing delays. IT leaders must distinguish between infrastructure and business resilience, mapping dependencies across zones and suppliers to identify single points of failure.

entries.title: NATO has a theory of victory – the EU needs one for Russia’s unconventional war on Europe
entries.summary: Discusses NATO's theory of victory versus the EU's need for strategy regarding Russia's unconventional warfare against Europe.

entries.title: Courts Are Striking Down Warrantless Flock Camera Use
entries.summary: Reports on courts striking down warrantless use of Flock cameras.

entries.title: AI Can (Mostly) Solve Cyber Regulatory Harmonization and Efficiency
entries.summary: Examines how artificial intelligence can address cyber regulatory harmonisation and efficiency challenges.

entries.title: Expanding Teen Account Protections to Teens Around the World
entries.summary: Meta is expanding AI-powered Teen Account protections globally across Instagram, Facebook and Messenger. The technology identifies suspected teens who misrepresent their age and automatically applies age-appropriate protections limiting contacts, content and screen time. Rolling out on Facebook and later Threads.

entries.summary: Covers contextual safeguarding approaches.

entries.summary: Provides guidance on responding to children displaying sexualised behaviour.

entries.summary: Ofcom strengthens industry guidance protecting participant welfare in constructed reality programmes.

entries.title: Oxford spinout, Fairwork, launches certification programme
entries.summary: Fairwork, an Oxford spinout, offers independent certification enabling organisations to demonstrate responsible labour practices across AI supply chains.

entries.title: Rebuilding trust and confidence after a critical incident: Lessons from the Plymouth mass shooting
entries.summary: Covers lessons on rebuilding trust and confidence in policing following critical incidents, using the Plymouth mass shooting as a case study.

entries.title: Working with children who display harmful sexual behaviour
entries.summary: Addresses policing approaches and best practices for working with children who display harmful sexual behaviour.

entries.title: New research aims to close the gaps on recognising, reporting and responding to female sex offending
entries.summary: Research examining gaps in recognising, reporting and responding to female sex offending within policing contexts.

entries.title: Westminster Insight’s AI in Policing Conference
entries.summary: Westminster Insight's conference focused on artificial intelligence applications and developments in policing.

entries.title: The Life of the Party(-State)
entries.summary: RAND researchers examine how China's political cycle and bureaucratic structures have shifted under Xi Jinping, affecting U.S.-China relations and American engagement strategies.
